newsitem.title: USA: Jamaica issues hurricane warning for Marco.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica issues hurricane warning for Marco.

text.p: The Jamaican government on Wednesday issued a hurricane warning and urged residents to prepare for rough weather as Hurricane Marco with its 75 mile-per-hour (120 kph) winds moved toward the island.

At 10 a.m. EST (1500 GMT), the centre of Marco was located 220 miles (354 km) south of Kingston, Jamaica, at latitude 14.8 north and longitude 77.2 west, the National Hurricane Centre in Miami said. A hurricane watch was issued for Haiti and the eastern portion of Cuba.

Marco was moving northeast at 9 mph (14 kph) and was expected to near the coast of Jamaica on Thursday, forecasters said. It was dumping torrential rain of up 10 inches (25 cm) in its path, which could cause mudslides and rockslides over the island, forecasters said.
"The storm is moving east now but we expect it to slow down and turn in a more northerly direction later today," hurricane forecaster Lixion Avila said.

On Tuesday, Nicaraguan civil defence authorities blamed at least two deaths on Marco after flooding washed away homes in the Pacific coast and northern regions. They said one person had died in a traffic accident and another by drowning.

Marco was upgraded from a tropical storm on Wednesday after a ship in the middle of the storm recorded sustained winds of 75 mph (120 kph), Avila said. It was a minimal hurricane capable of flooding coastal roads and causing minor wind damage.
A tropical storm graduates to hurricane status when its maximum winds exceed 74 mph (119 kph). This year's Atlantic hurricane season officially ends on Nov. 30.
